result.title: Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as formalizers: given a reasoning problem expressed in natural language, they produce a formal specification that a symbolic solver can then solve, with guarantees relative to that specification. Many specifications are runnable yet semantically wrong, encoding incorrect constraints, domains, objectives, predicates, or goals, and solver-error feedback dries up once execution succeeds. Purely LLM-based diagnosis, lacking a formal ground truth, often fails to spot these errors, and its ungrounded critiques cause regressions in 11.8% of initially correct specifications in our experiments. We propose DRAGO, a repair framework that replaces this ungrounded critique with deterministic, formalism-specific diagnosis, and retains a rewrite only when the diagnosed error weight strictly decreases under a reference-free acceptance predicate. Across five benchmarks spanning logical reasoning (SMT-LIB2), constraint programming (MiniZinc), and planning (PDDL), DRAGO cuts regressions by nearly an order of magnitude, to 1.3%, while improving answer accuracy by 12.9 percentage points over zero-shot formalization and 8.7 percentage points over LLM-diagnostic repair, averaged across benchmarks. We also uncover two rendering defects in Planetarium that cause 50% (3,086 instances) of its floor-tile split to be inconsistent with the reference formalizations, and release a corrected split.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 DRAGO 修复框架：用确定性、针对具体形式系统的诊断替代无依据的 LLM 自我批评，仅在诊断误差权重严格下降时保留重写，在 SMT-LIB2、MiniZinc、PDDL 五个基准上显著减少回归并提升答案准确率，同时指出 Planetarium 的渲染缺陷。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「无参考接受准则＋误差严格下降才保留改写」的验证与筛选机制，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 推理状态更新与答案修正的接受、验证与回归控制方式。该工作不涉及视觉或多模态推理，属纯文本形式化修复。
